answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the wander check immediately, the tundra audit keeps the resolved set and the dune replay reveals exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 130 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 130 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
